en: Mahāśītavatī: Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Mahāśītavatī!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagṛha.
In the great cremation ground of Śītavana, in the vicinity of the Iṅghikā shrine, the Venerable Rāhula was being excessively tormented there by celestial spirits,
nāga spirits, yakṣa spirits, rākṣasa spirits, marut spirits, asura spirits,
kinnara spirits, garuḍa spirits, gandharva spirits, mahoraga spirits, human spirits, non-human spirits, and preta spirits.
[He was surrounded] by *bhūta*-grahas, *piśāca*-grahas, *kumbhāṇḍa*-grahas, by leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and other beings, both human and non-human.

Then the venerable Rāhula approached the place where the Blessed One was; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and [stood] before the Blessed One.
Weeping, he shed tears.
Then the Blessed One, though already knowing [the reason], addressed Rāhula:
"Rāhula, why do you stand before me weeping and shedding tears?"
When this had been said, the Venerable Rāhula addressed the Blessed One:
"Here, Blessed One, I was dwelling at Rājagṛha in the Śītavana great cemetery, in the vicinity of the Iṅghikāyatana.
There, Blessed One, I was harassed."

By the seizers of gods, seizers of nāgas, seizers of yakṣas, seizers of rākṣasas, seizers of maruts, seizers of asuras, seizers of kinnaras, seizers of garuḍas, seizers of gandharvas, seizers of mahoragas, seizers of humans, seizers of non-humans, seizers of pretas, seizers of bhūtas,
seizers of piśācas, seizers of kumbhāṇḍas, by leopards, crows, owls, insects, and reptiles.
And by other beings, both human and non-human.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Rāhula: "Rāhula, you should take up this spell and knowledge called Mahāśītavatī,
for the protection, defense, and guardianship of the fourfold assembly— of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen— and for the long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness of all sentient beings."
It will lead to security and well-being.
Namely: Aṅgas, Vaṅgas,
Kaliṅgas, Varaṅgas, Saṃsārataraṅgas, and Sāsadaṅgas.
The Bhagas are the Asuras;
the Ekataṅgas are the Asura-vīras; the Taras are the Vīras.
Tara tara vīrā! Kara vīrā! Kara kara vīrā!
Indrā and Indrakisarā; Haṃsā and Haṃsakisarā; Picimālā.
Mahākiccā, Viheṭhikā, Kālucchikā, Aṅgodarā, Jayālikā.
Velā cintāli / cili cili hili hili sumati vasumati / culu naṭṭe /
culu culu naṭṭe / culu culu culu naṭṭe / culu nāḍi /
Ku nāḍi / hārīṭaki hārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki / gauri gandhāri /
Caṇḍālī, Vetālī,
Mātaṅgī,
Varcasī, Dharaṇī, Dhāraṇī!
O Savior, O Deliverer!
O you who wear a necklace of camels!
O Kaca, O Kācikī!
O Kaca! O Kācive! O Cala! O Nāṭike! O Kākalike!
Lalamati, Lakṣamati, Varāhakula.
Matpale utpale / Kara vīre / Kara kara vīre /
Tara vīre / tara tara vīre / kuru vīre /
Kuru kuru vīre!
Curu vīre! Curu curu vīre!
O Great Hero! O Irāmatī!
O Varāmatī!
Rakṣamati / Sarvārthasādhani / Paramārthasādhani.
O Unobstructed One!
Indra is king;
Yama is king.
King Varuṇa; King Kubera; King Manasvin.
King Vāsukī,
King Daṇḍakī,
and King Daṇḍāgni.
King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, King Virūḍhaka, and King Virūpākṣa.
Brahmā is a king who is the sovereign of a thousand worlds;
the Buddha, the Blessed One, is a king who is the Lord of Dharma,
the unsurpassed one who has compassion for the world.
May they grant protection for me and for all sentient beings;

may they provide defense, rescue, shelter, guardianship, peace, well-being, exemption from punishment, exemption from weapons, the neutralization of poison, the destruction of poison, the binding of boundaries, and the binding of the earth; and may they live for a hundred years.
May they behold [it] for a hundred autumns.
They are as follows: Ilā, Milā, Utpalā,
Iramati, Viramati, and Halamati.
Talamati, Kṣalamati, Lakṣamati, Rakṣamati.
Kuru kuru mati!
Huru huru phuru phuru cara (Mś_4) cara khara khara khuru khuru mati mati bhūmicaṇḍe!
Kālike!
Abhisaṃlāpite!
Sāmalate!
Hūle sthūle! O you of massive peaks! Victory to you, O Stūle!
O Victorious One!
O Valanaṭṭe!
Move through the channels, gulp down the channel, gulp down the channel, O binder of speech!
O you who cause growth!
O blood-relation!
O dark one, O pale one!
Karāle, Kinnare, Keyūre, Ketumati!
O you who have gone to the realm of beings, O you whose mind is fixed on reality!
O auspicious one, O bringer of blessings!
O Golden Womb!
O you of great power! O you whose root is Avalokita! O you who are immovable and fierce!
O bearer of the yoke, O victorious one, O you who have gone beyond victory, O you who have ascended to victory!
Curu curu! Phuru phuru! Bind, bind! Support, support! Sustain, sustain! O obstructress! O destroyer! O annihilator!
O binder! O liberator! O one who releases! O releaser! O one who sets free!
Deluding, utterly deluding; manifesting, utterly manifesting; purifying, thoroughly purifying, completely purifying, universally purifying.
The disperser,
the scatterer,
the cutter asunder.
Sādhu turamāṇe!
Hara hara bandhumati! Hiri hiri khiri khiri kharali!
Huru huru khuru khuru, homage be to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, svāhā!

Furthermore, Rāhula, if one ties a knot in this *Mahāśītavatī* spell of one hundred and ten words found in the sutra, and carries it on one's hand or wears it around one's neck, protection will be established for a hundred leagues in every direction.
Neither humans nor non-humans shall prevail over one by means of perfumes, flowers, or seals.
Neither by weapon, nor poison, nor disease, nor fever, nor high fever, nor spells and mantras, nor by a vetāḍa;

neither by illness, nor fire, nor poison and water will he meet his end. It brings success to all applications of spells and mantras, whether they have been properly employed or were previously unsuccessful.
It agitates the perfected ones,
binds those employed by others,
and liberates those who are bound by others.
It is the destroyer of all diseases, sorrows, obstacles, and Vināyakas;
it is the pacifier of the defilements of strife and contention.
If any planetary spirit does not release [the person], its head shall split into seven pieces like the cluster of an Arjaka flower.

And Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, would strike him with his vajra—blazing, aflame, and become a single mass of fire—until it shatters his head. Furthermore, the four Great Kings would shatter his head with an iron wheel and destroy him with a stroke like the edge of a razor; thus he would fall from that world of the yakṣas.
He does not find lodging in the capital city of Aḍakavatī.

Furthermore, Rāhula, when this Great Śītavatī Great Vidyā is recited even once, one who has fallen into the midst of kings, thieves, water, fire, poison, weapons, forests, or wildernesses is completely liberated from all fears.

Indeed, this Great Śītavatī Vidyā has been spoken, will be spoken, and is being spoken by ninety-one Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; it is accomplished, supremely accomplished, and possesses accomplished prowess.
Having been worshipped by all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and others, and surrounded by the assembly of all the Victors,

protect me and all sentient beings from all fears and calamities! May there always be auspiciousness, health, and fearlessness at all times, in every way, from every quarter, and in all circumstances!

Thus spoke the Blessed One; and the venerable Rāhula, the entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened One, had said.
The Noble Queen of Spells named Mahāśītavatī is completed.
